Flooding Disrupts Thai Logistics Hubs, Forces Site Evacuations and Halts Operations

BANGKOK, June 14 — Severe flooding triggered by days of torrential rain has inundated multiple logistics depots and distribution centers in Thailand’s central Chao Phraya basin, prompting emergency shutdowns and evacuations across the sector, industry officials said Friday.

The deluge, which began Tuesday and is ongoing, has seen floodwaters rise to over 1.5 meters in the Bang Pa-in and Wang Noi districts, home to some of the country’s largest warehousing complexes and cross-docking facilities. Industry sources said at least eight major sites operated by leading transportation and logistics providers have been forced to suspend activities, with water entering storage areas and truck yards.

“Floodwater entered our Bang Pa-in logistics park early Thursday, forcing us to halt all operations and evacuate more than 200 staff,” said Chaiyut Rattanaphong, spokesperson for Eastern Gateway Logistics. “Our priority is ensuring the safety of workers and securing high-value goods.”

The Thai Logistics Association (TLA) said the immediate impact includes damage to facilities, vehicles, and stored inventory, as well as disruptions to site-based cargo handling and warehouse management. “Initial reports indicate that hundreds of workers have been displaced, and companies are working to provide temporary shelter and food,” TLA chairman Nopparat Jiraratana said.

Experts say flood protection barriers installed after past events have been overwhelmed by the intensity of the rainfall, which the Meteorological Department described as the heaviest in a decade for the region. “Many logistics hubs are built on low-lying land for transport access, making them particularly vulnerable,” noted Voranuch Suwannarat, an independent industry analyst.

With water levels still rising, site managers are pumping out floodwater and moving salvageable cargo to higher ground. “We are monitoring the situation hour by hour,” said Jiraratana. “The safety of our workers and the preservation of assets remain our top concern as the event continues to unfold.”
